checks.evidence: The saved native frame shows a soft face shape, dark eyes, wispy forehead fringe and short jaw-length dark bob close to the supplied portrait. Clothing and camera angle differ as authored. This is an appearance comparison, not proof of identity or age.

Warm wall-mounted flame fixtures, timber drawers, hand tools, brass vessel base and blouse/bodice occupy the same photographed room as the pale translucent hand inside a closed clear bell. These are period-coded visible cues; fuel chemistry, authentic date and real supernatural cause are not inferred.

The human index finger and pale-blue inner index finger both lead toward the same bright frost-star region at roughly image x815,y500. However, the saturated white center covers the final fingertip contours and local separating glass boundary. Exact inner/outer fingertip meeting through the same wall cannot be resolved from this single saved frame. UNOBSERVABLE_NOT_PASS; partial_is_fail.

A narrow repaired vertical seam with small metallic bridges runs down the bell. White branching frost is visibly continuous around the luminous contact region and branches cross that seam. This supports the authored visible frost-over-seam arrangement, not elapsed repair history or a measured thermal process.

The reaching human right hand continues through wrist and forearm to its sleeved arm, which meets the bench; the other hand rests separately near the brass base. The spectral hand remains a distinct vaporous hand inside the vessel. No major contradictory reach or owner transfer is visible.

strict_reason: The intended contact endpoints and separating glass wall are not all assessable in the overbright contact core. A plausible overall impression does not replace complete endpoint evidence.
genre_readability: The image strongly reads as a tangible nineteenth-century-style craft workshop inhabited by an impossible spectral presence.

strengths: Face, short bob, fingertip and glass bell form a clear visual hierarchy.
Warm flame lighting and cool translucent hand share coherent depth and reflections.
Repair case, hand tools and coiled wire make the craft context legible without a caption.
Natural skin, wool, glass and worn brass support a convincing photographic register.
limits: The exact glass-separated meeting is hidden by the glow.
The visible hand does not prove an entity's real identity, life state or motive; workshop props do not certify occupation or historical date.
No before-after photograph exists to prove the repair sequence.
